decision: Use public benchmarks as bounded stress tests inside an intended-use evidence ladder. No public benchmark score can establish zero harm, local clinical efficacy, or deployment readiness.

systemUnderTest.intendedUser: licensed clinician or clinical operations reviewer
systemUnderTest.input: bounded active-episode asynchronous patient message transcript
systemUnderTest.output: four-level operational disposition plus an optional bounded clinician handoff; the supplied three-level task is retained through an explicit legacy projection

allowedNow: The checked-in deterministic software artifacts satisfy their specified synthetic contracts when the repository validation suite passes.
The frozen synthetic retrieval candidate was not admitted after failing its preregistered temporal-holdout thresholds.
The repository contains an executable, attributable single-clinician development-review instrument.
claimPolicy.publicBenchmarkRule: A benchmark may support only the capability and test distribution it directly measures. It cannot satisfy an intended-use clinical, human-factors, operational, or patient-outcome gate by itself.

benchmarkPortfolio.name: HealthBench
controls: Do not publish examples in plaintext or screenshots.
Disable web access and benchmark retrieval during inference.
Keep a separately governed private local holdout for leakage detection.
Do not translate a four-level route label or its three-level legacy projection into an official HealthBench score.
limitations: Most example-specific criteria were authored by one physician and not independently validated.
Per-example rubrics are not comprehensive.
Model-physician and physician-physician grading agreement is imperfect.
It evaluates responses, not this V0's local workflow or patient outcomes.

benchmarkPortfolio.name: HealthBench Consensus
requiredReporting: adaptation mapping and deviations from the official task
controls: Call any route-label adaptation a local derived evaluation, not an official HealthBench score.
Pre-register which criteria map to the route contract before inspecting candidate outputs.
Keep conditional emergencies and unconditional emergencies as separate strata.
limitations: Higher precision comes with lower recall for possible failures.
Consensus criteria are narrow behavior checks, not a complete clinical reference.

benchmarkPortfolio.name: HealthBench Hard
measures: performance on 1,000 examples selected for frontier-model difficulty
controls: Never use HealthBench Hard as the clinical safety gate.
Report that difficulty selection is model-relative and not harm-severity selection.
limitations: The subset was selected for model difficulty, not intended-use prevalence or clinical harm.
A high score can coexist with rare severe failures.

benchmarkPortfolio.name: First, do NOHARM v2
requiredReporting: results by management-action category and specialty
judge model snapshots and cache namespace
controls: Use the official open kit without copying cases or rubrics into this repository.
Run base cases and perturbations; preserve base-case clustering in intervals.
Treat omission and commission separately and retain the severe-harm rate outside any average.
Use a new cache namespace whenever model outputs or model IDs change.
Report the open-subset result separately from private-leaderboard evaluation.
limitations: The public kit contains 30 base cases; the full evaluation includes a private set.
It grades free-text management plans, which this V0 does not produce.
The judge uses preview model versions that can drift.
Absolute scores and harm rates are rubric indicators for the selected cases, not real-world event rates.
The text-only, single-turn consult task omits chart navigation, multimodal inputs, and full clinical workflow.

benchmarkPortfolio.name: MedAgentBench
benchmarkPortfolio.activationCondition: The product can read or mutate an EHR through FHIR-like tools.
controls: Reset or isolate state between action trials.
Add authorization, idempotency, rollback, and audit checks that the public environment does not provide.
Record both intended action correctness and actual committed world state.
Do not convert repeated sampling into a best-of-k deployment claim.
limitations: The original baseline used only GET requests during evaluation to avoid costly environment restarts.
The environment explicitly lacks production security and enterprise logging.
Profiles come from one academic medical center and are not population-representative.
Task instructions and exact-output graders simplify real clinical coordination and ambiguity.

benchmarkPortfolio.name: MedAgentBench v2
benchmarkPortfolio.activationCondition: The product has FHIR tools or a governed cross-episode memory proposal.
requiredReporting: category, complexity, latency, and cost slices
controls: Never write a test answer or failed-test correction into memory used on the same evaluation partition.
Version every memory with source, author, review status, and revocation path.
Require physician approval for clinical memories and test negative transfer.
Constrain calculators and tools independently; do not rely on prompting as the sandbox.
limitations: The reported 98% used memories synthesized from failures on the original task family.
High task success does not establish safe real-world interpretation of terse, ambiguous instructions.
Rigid output grading can mark clinically correct reasoning wrong and still miss unmodeled clinical harm.

benchmarkPortfolio.name: HealthAgentBench
benchmarkPortfolio.activationCondition: The product performs terminal-style multimodal, ETL, audit, trial-matching, or longitudinal EHR tasks.
controls: Disable web search and fetching during evaluation.
Isolate fetched gold labels from the agent environment.
Treat each category as a separate construct instead of relying only on a pooled mean.
limitations: The 54 tasks span heterogeneous constructs and modalities outside this V0.
Several categories require gated clinical datasets and at least 30 GB of assets.
Pooled task success is not a routing-safety or efficacy measure.

benchmarkPortfolio.name: MedSafe-Dx v0
benchmarkPortfolio.activationCondition: Use only after confirming license compatibility and freezing an output adapter that preserves the benchmark construct.
requiredReporting: all safety event counts outside aggregate effectiveness
clinical review of every safety failure
controls: Do not modify or redistribute the benchmark under its CC BY-NC-ND license.
Do not treat synthetic diagnostic cases as an intended-use estimate.
Retain every severe event outside averages.
limitations: It is a 2026 preprint and v0 benchmark.
It is built from DDXPlus synthetic diagnostic cases rather than Counsel's inbox distribution.
Its license restricts commercial use and derivatives.

metrics: same-day and emergency miss hypotheses confirmed or rejected

requiredEvidence: preregistered intended population, routes, destinations, and SLA
untouched patient- and episode-independent representative sample
blinded reference process with calibrated multi-clinician overlap
all exclusions, denominators, sampling weights, and intervals
metrics: emergency and same-day sensitivity and positive predictive value reported separately, plus any-escalation performance
one-sided exact upper bound after zero observed severe under-triage events
abstention and calibration when scores are emitted
performance by age, language, site, access context, and time

requiredEvidence: realistic queue pressure, interruptions, and degraded-system drills
analysis of automation bias and alert fatigue
metrics: completed escalation rather than predicted route

requiredEvidence: governance, privacy, security, and incident-response approval
silent prospective run with no autonomous patient-facing or EHR action
predefined stop rules and rollback drills
approved protocol matched to risk and intended use
DECIDE-AI reporting for early live evaluation
SPIRIT-AI and CONSORT-AI reporting when an interventional trial is warranted
metrics: patient safety events and near misses
patient-reported comprehension or experience when applicable

requiredEvidence: change control and versioned release evidence
metrics: distribution, provider, prompt, tool, and retrieval drift

beforeAnyPaidRun: Freeze system prompt, tool schemas, retrieval corpus, model snapshot, judge snapshot, seeds, and output adapter.
Confirm construct compatibility; do not score a route label as if it were a management plan or patient response.
Estimate the full inference and judging cost and set provider-side hard limits.
Pre-register primary, safety, subgroup, and failure-analysis metrics.
Separate development, public benchmark, private holdout, and intended-use results.
afterAnyRun: Archive immutable prompts, traces, tool calls, raw outputs, grader decisions, hashes, versions, latency, and cost.
Review every severe or potentially severe failure clinically.
Run grader meta-evaluation and adjudicate disagreements before publishing a score.
Do not tune on the private local holdout; start a newly registered candidate if changes are made.

governingSources.name: IMDRF SaMD Clinical Evaluation N41
governingSources.use: Separate valid clinical association, analytical validation, and clinical validation; treat evaluation as continuous and risk-proportionate.

governingSources.name: IMDRF/FDA Good Machine Learning Practice
governingSources.use: Apply total-product-lifecycle discipline, representative data, human-AI performance, monitoring, and managed retraining risk as engineering principles.

governingSources.name: DECIDE-AI
governingSources.use: Design and report early live clinical evaluation around actual performance, safety, and human factors.

governingSources.name: SPIRIT-AI and CONSORT-AI
governingSources.use: Pre-specify and transparently report prospective interventional trials, human-AI interaction, inputs, outputs, and error cases.

governingSources.name: NIST AI RMF 1.0
governingSources.use: Govern, map, measure, and manage safety, validity, security, privacy, transparency, and harmful bias in context.
